channel.title: Centinel on Anti-Federalist Library
channel.description: Recent content in Centinel on Anti-Federalist Library

item.title: Centinel I
item.description: Warns that centralizing power in the federal government undermines state authority and individual freedoms.

item.title: Centinel II
item.description: Argues that a large republic cannot effectively protect the rights and interests of its citizens.

item.title: Centinel III
item.description: Rejects the need for a new constitution, arguing that state governments are capable of maintaining order and governance.

item.title: Centinel IV
item.description: Criticizes the proposed judiciary for granting the federal government excessive control over legal matters.

item.title: Centinel V
item.description: Highlights the lack of a Bill of Rights as a major oversight, leaving citizens vulnerable to government abuse.

item.title: Centinel VI
item.description: Explores how centralizing power erodes state autonomy and weakens local self-governance.

item.title: Centinel VII
item.description: Warns that federal taxation policies will unfairly burden the states, particularly those with agricultural economies.

item.title: Centinel VIII
item.description: Raises concerns about federal control of commerce, potentially disadvantaging local industries and empowering monopolies.

item.title: Centinel IX
item.description: Criticizes vague constitutional language, fearing it will allow the federal government to expand its power unchecked.

item.title: Centinel X
item.description: Calls for amending the Articles of Confederation rather than adopting a new, untested system.

item.title: Centinel XI
item.description: Urges rejection of the Constitution, arguing that its adoption would undermine liberty and state sovereignty.

item.title: Centinel XII
item.description: Argues that the new Constitution grants excessive power to the national government, threatening state sovereignty and individual liberties.

item.title: Centinel XII
item.description: Critiques the Senate’s structure as aristocratic, with unequal representation and concentrated power.

item.title: Centinel XIV
item.description: Rejects the notion that the Constitution’s checks and balances will prevent tyranny, fearing it will empower a central government.

item.title: Centinel XV
item.description: Criticizes the lack of a Bill of Rights, claiming it invites government overreach and threatens individual freedoms.

item.title: Centinel XVI
item.description: Warns that the strong federal judiciary would undermine state courts and give the national government undue influence over local matters.

item.title: Centinel XVII
item.description: Claims the Constitution would erode state legislatures’ powers, subordinating them to the federal government.

item.title: Centinel XVIII
item.description: Calls for the rejection of the Constitution, arguing it is fundamentally flawed and will lead to dangerous centralization.
